key_terms.meaning: a ≡ b (mod n) means n divides a − b; both leave the same remainder on division by n.
Positive integer n that fixes the remainder range 0,1,…,n−1.
Largest positive integer d with d | a and d | b.
Integers a,b with gcd(a,b)=1.
Repeated division algorithm that returns gcd(a,b).
Euclidean algorithm plus back-substitution; returns gcd(a,b) and integers x,y with ax+by=gcd(a,b).
a⁻¹ mod n satisfies a·a⁻¹ ≡ 1 (mod n); it exists iff gcd(a,n)=1.
Set with an associative operation, an identity, and an inverse for every element.
Set with addition and multiplication obeying ring axioms; multiplication need not have inverses.
Commutative ring in which every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse.
GF(p) = {0,1,…,p−1} with addition and multiplication modulo prime p.
Integer p>1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and p.
Algorithm that decides whether an integer is prime or composite without finding its factors.
φ(n) counts integers k with 1≤k≤n and gcd(k,n)=1.
For prime p and p∤a, a^(p−1) ≡ 1 (mod p).
For gcd(a,n)=1, a^φ(n) ≡ 1 (mod n).
For coprime moduli n₁,…,n_k, x≡a_i (mod n_i) has one solution modulo n₁⋯n_k.
a is a quadratic residue mod p if x²≡a (mod p) has a solution x.
(a/p)=1 if a is a nonzero QR, −1 if a is a nonresidue, and 0 if p|a.
Jacobi symbol (a/n) is the product of Legendre symbols (a/p_i) over prime factors p_i of odd n.

takeaways: Two integers are congruent modulo n exactly when n divides their difference, so arithmetic can use remainders from 0 to n−1.
The Euclidean algorithm finds gcd by repeated remainder; the extended version also gives a modular inverse when gcd is 1.
A field supplies addition, subtraction, multiplication and division by nonzero elements, which is what many public-key formulas need.
Large primes are chosen randomly and tested; a primality test answers prime or composite without factoring the number.
Fermat and Euler theorems let you reduce large exponents modulo p or φ(n), which makes modular exponentiation practical.
The Chinese remainder theorem turns one congruence modulo a product into smaller independent congruences and back again.
Quadratic residues detect squares modulo p; Legendre and Jacobi symbols test this by calculation rather than listing squares.
A modular inverse exists only for coprime numbers, a condition that underlies RSA key setup and many cryptographic steps.
bank_note: Long answers usually ask for definitions, a proof or justification of the number-theory result, and a worked cryptographic computation such as an inverse, a modular exponent, or a CRT reconstruction.

bank.q: Define congruence modulo n and prove that a≡b (mod n) if and only if n divides a−b. List the residue classes modulo 7.
State the Euclidean algorithm and explain why replacing (a,b) by (b,a mod b) preserves the gcd. Use it to find gcd(1071,462).
Define group, ring and field. Show that Z_p is a field when p is prime and explain why Z_n is only a ring when n is composite.
State Fermat's little theorem, Euler's theorem and the definition of φ(n). Explain how each theorem reduces a large exponent modulo n.
outline: exponent reduction by p−1 or φ(n)

bank.q: Use the extended Euclidean algorithm on 240 and 46. Find gcd(240,46) and integers x,y with 240x+46y=gcd(240,46).
Find 37⁻¹ modulo 101 using the extended Euclidean algorithm. Check the answer by multiplication.
Solve the system x≡1 (mod 5), x≡2 (mod 7), x≡3 (mod 11) using the Chinese remainder theorem.
Test 97 for primality by trial division and by the Fermat test with base 2. State what each test proves and does not prove.
outline: Fermat pass is evidence, not proof of primality

bank.q: Explain why Carmichael numbers defeat the simple Fermat test. Use 561=3·11·17 to illustrate the idea.
Prove that a system of congruences with pairwise coprime moduli has a unique solution modulo their product. Evaluate why this uniqueness matters in CRT-based computation.
outline: uniqueness by difference divisible by product

bank.q: Compare the Legendre and Jacobi symbols. Show why a Jacobi symbol equal to 1 does not always mean a quadratic residue.
outline: QR test needs prime modulus or extra step

bank.q: Prove Euler's theorem from the group of units modulo n. Evaluate how it justifies reducing exponents modulo φ(n) in modular exponentiation.
Design the key-generation steps for RSA: choose primes, test them, compute n and φ(n), choose e, and find d. Explain which number-theory result guarantees d exists.
Explain how finite fields, the Chinese remainder theorem and quadratic residues appear in public-key cryptography. Include one worked modular step for RSA, CRT decryption, or Rabin encryption.

glossary.def: Arithmetic in which numbers are reduced to remainders modulo a fixed integer.
The relation a≡b (mod n), meaning n divides a−b.
The fixed positive integer n used in a congruence or remainder system.
The remainder r in 0≤r<n when an integer is divided by n.
The largest positive integer that divides both given integers.
Two integers whose greatest common divisor is 1.
A repeated-remainder method that computes the greatest common divisor of two integers.
The Euclidean algorithm plus back-substitution, producing Bézout coefficients and modular inverses.
The equation ax+by=gcd(a,b) for suitable integers x and y.
An integer a⁻¹ such that a·a⁻¹≡1 (mod n), existing exactly when gcd(a,n)=1.
A set with one operation that is closed, associative, has an identity, and has inverses.
A group whose operation is commutative.
A set with addition and multiplication satisfying the distributive and additive group laws.
A commutative ring in which every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse.
A field with finitely many elements; GF(p) has p elements for prime p.
An integer greater than 1 with no positive divisors other than 1 and itself.
An integer greater than 1 that is not prime.
An algorithm that answers prime or composite for a given integer.
φ(n) counts the integers from 1 to n that are coprime to n.
For prime p and a not divisible by p, a^(p−1)≡1 (mod p).
For gcd(a,n)=1, a^φ(n)≡1 (mod n).
A system of congruences with coprime moduli has a unique solution modulo their product.
An integer a that equals some square x² modulo p.
(a/p) records whether a is a quadratic residue, nonresidue, or zero modulo odd prime p.
A generalization of the Legendre symbol to odd composite moduli by multiplying over prime factors.
For odd prime p and p∤a, a^((p−1)/2)≡(a/p) (mod p).
